newsitem.title: CHINA: China futures company fined for fraudulent trading.
newsitem.headline: China futures company fined for fraudulent trading.

text.p: China's securities authorities have punished a futures company for fraudulent trading, forcing the firm to cease operations for six months, the Shanghai Securities News reported on Saturday.
The newspaper said the company, Jinma Futures, had cheated clients of money by giving them false information about the amounts and prices of contracts traded on their behalf.
The firm, based in eastern Zhejiang province, faked several trading reports for customers, particularly trades in green bean futures on the Beijing and Zhengzhou futures exchanges.
The China Securities Regulatory Commisssion (CSRC) said in a statement that Jinma's fraudulent activity had had a serious impact on the futures markets.

It ordered Jinma to stop operating for six months and to undergo "re-organisation". Its open positions in the market, either on its own account or on behalf of clients must be closed off as soon as possible, it said.
The Shanghai Securities News said the action against Jinma showed authorities' determination to clean up the futures market.
"The clean-up activities have already achieved some success, but there can be no relaxation. People who violate the market rules must be punished harshly," the newspaper commentary said.
